page: Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is a graphics-intensive virtual machine instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with 2 threads per core) running at 3.4 GHz, alongside 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. For hardware acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 250 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The instance achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference, delivering 13365.51 tokens per second for small model prompt processing and 134.56 tokens per second for medium model text generation. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is weak, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, registering weak read-only and write speeds on large blocks. Single-core CPU performance remains average to strong, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g6e.xlarge offers high resource density for GPU-centric workloads, trading off raw multi-core CPU capacity and memory bandwidth for specialized Ada Lovelace acceleration. This hardware profile is suited for small to medium LLM inference, graphics-intensive rendering, and GPU-accelerated machine learning tasks, while it is less optimal for CPU-heavy compilation, database operations, or high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.xlarge is a graphics-intensive instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 4 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It features a dedicated NVIDIA L40S GPU with 45 GB of VRAM and a 250 GB NVMe SSD. While multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%, the instance delivers top-tier results in LLM inference, achieving 6130.77 tokens per second for medium model prompt processing. This makes the g6e.xlarge highly cost-efficient for specialized GPU workloads, such as machine learning inference and graphics rendering, rather than general-purpose multi-core computing or database operations.
